key_insight: APS-produced Fe79Zr6Si14Cu1 coatings remained predominantly crystalline despite rapid cooling, while increasing spray distance improved hardness and wear resistance at the expense of corrosion resistance.
engineering_relevance: Spray distance provides a practical lever for balancing mechanical durability and corrosion performance, with 90 mm offering the most favourable balance among the tested conditions.
method: Deposit low-glass-forming-ability Fe79Zr6Si14Cu1 coatings by atmospheric plasma spraying at varied spray distances.
Characterize phase constitution, lamellar microstructure and porosity.
Evaluate hardness, wear resistance and electrochemical behaviour.
evidence_signal: XRD detected α-Fe(Si) and Fe–Zr intermetallic phases but no amorphous fraction; porosity ranged from 2.2% to 4.9%, and the 90 mm coating showed the best reported property balance.
watch_item: The 90 mm result is specific to the tested conditions; longer spray distances increased porosity and interlamellar defects, compromising corrosion resistance.
paper_title: Phase Evolution and Structure–Property Relationships of Fe79Zr6Si14Cu1 Coatings with Low GFA Produced by Atmospheric Plasma Spraying
